kind: mid-work adversarial review, after the instruments were built and verified by violation
whatChangedSinceCP1: The artboard count fell from the CP1 plan in one place and held in the others: Fire and EMS ships TWO boards, not three. The station partition is the lens design argument and it earns full width on Main rather than a board of its own, and an ungranted board would have repeated a sentence the Public works Empty board already draws. Padding to match another folder's board count is not a reason to draw one.

The phase-against-status matrix was TRANSPOSED after rendering. The first draft had status as the row and phase as the column, and 'construction' ran into 'closeout' on the rendered board at 452px. Phase names are the long ones and a row label has room. Rendering found it; re-reading the generator would not have.

A provenance foot was added to every Public works and Fire and EMS board, naming the domain id, the vendor kind and the record type in the product's own codes. Two reasons: a staff member on a page that will not fill needs to know whose feed is missing, and check.mjs needs real codes to compare against the registry. Without it the check matched ZERO domain/gate pairs on two of four boards and said so.
The Parks unblock panel moved from the left column to the rail, and both columns were tightened, after the rendered board showed content past the bottom edge.

defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.defect: A money token reached the money-free lens.
defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.found: check.mjs, on the first run against real artboards
defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.detail: The boards wrote 'per cent' as two words. The product's own money gate (FORBIDDEN_CONTENT in src/fixture-seam.mjs, copied verbatim into the check) matches the standalone word 'cent', so British two-word spelling trips the product's own rule. The product writes 'percent'. Fixed in the generator, and the finding is reported because it applies to every surface, not just this one.

defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.defect: The instrument read the inlined stylesheet as page content.
defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.detail: textOf() stripped tags but not <style> blocks, so CSS token names entered every content rule. A control whose scope is broader than its claim. Fixed in all three checks and pinned by a self-test in both directions.

defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.defect: The first check could not read the registry at all.
defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.found: the check's own self-test, on its first run
defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.detail: It built its allowlist from d.domainId; listDomains() returns d.id. The set came back empty and every pair would have passed vacuously. The self-test failed and the file refused to report a verdict. A guard was added that exits 2 when the registry yields no domains for the lens, so the same shape cannot recur silently.

defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.defect: The twelfth apparatus was clipped while the basis line claimed twelve of twelve.
defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.detail: The generator was correct and the board was wrong. A readiness screen showing eleven of twelve units is the exact case where the missing rows are the ones somebody is looking for. Row padding tightened; all twelve now render.

defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.defect: The nav foot claimed three live grants on a lens that has two regions.
defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.found: reading the rendered Blocked board against the registry
defectsThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.detail: Bastrop grants seven adapters in total; this lens has two. A figure a reader would have quoted.

verifiedByViolation.method: scripts in the session scratchpad break a REAL artboard on disk, run that folder's check.mjs, record the exit code, then restore by re-running gen.mjs and confirm the file is byte-identical to before
verifiedByViolation.oneViolationThatDidNotCount: An eighth Parks attempt replaced the first 'Not built' badge in the file, which sits in the NAV, outside the scoped page body. The check ignored it, which is the scoping working as designed rather than a miss. Re-aimed inside data-lens-body="parks", it was caught. A violation that misses its target is not evidence either way, and scoring it as a pass would have been the more dangerous mistake.
verifiedByViolation.excludedFromCounts: Every artboard mutation made by the violation harness is excluded from the design by construction: gen.mjs rewrites the board from source after each run and the harness fails if the restored file differs from the original.

nonVacuity.rule: every predicate reports a matched-input count and the file exits 2 if any matched zero across every board
nonVacuity.publicWorks: pairs=14, badges=77, cells=69, numbers=188, cipIds=10, queueRefs=11, statuses=2, verbatim=8 of 8 composer sentences
nonVacuity.fireEms: pairs=4, badges=37, bandChips=12, cells=72, numbers=116, unitIds=12, stationRefs=15, verbatim=5 of 5 composer sentences
nonVacuity.parks: bodies=2, badges=3, cells=41, fonts=97, rosterRows=5, builtSurfaceTermsOnContrast=8

openAtCP2: Naming the vendor on a lens panel is a change from what ships and needs an operator ruling before build.
The peer-region switcher on Public works is a change from the stacked layout that ships and needs the same ruling.

Whether any of the three vendors answers today is unestablished; the 2026-09-03 readings recorded in src/vendor-live.mjs are the only evidence in the repository and are badged as recorded, with their date, on the boards.
